proposal: The Mandate says the Economic Development Administration (EDA) duplicates other grant programs and should be abolished with its money moved elsewhere, or failing that have decisions centralized in the Assistant Secretary's office and use direct-hire authority. For the Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA), it accepts that Congress made the agency permanent in 2021 and recommends keeping it but refocusing it on policy analysis, tighter oversight of business centers, data and private-sector partnerships.
remaining: Congress would need to eliminate or defund EDA and change the Minority Business Development Act of 2021 for a closure of either agency; FY2027 appropriations are unenacted and continuing resolutions are pending.
Outcome of any appeal of the 2025-11-21 permanent injunction: not found in the sources reviewed.
EDA consolidation of decisions in the Assistant Secretary's office and use of direct-hire authority: not verified.

MBDA refocus on policy analysis and oversight of business centers (the Mandate's alternative to closure): not verified; the actions reported are closure-oriented and are the subject of the injunction.

status_summary: The administration has sought to close both agencies, which goes further than the Mandate on MBDA (where the Mandate accepted permanence and recommended refocusing). Executive Order 14238 (signed 2025-03-14) directed MBDA and six other entities, but not EDA, to be cut to the statutory minimum; the District of Rhode Island enjoined that directive for MBDA by preliminary injunction on 2025-05-13 and, on 2025-11-21, granted summary judgment vacating the order's implementation as to MBDA and three other agencies and permanently enjoining further implementation. The FY2026 and FY2027 budget requests propose closing EDA and MBDA, but P.L. 119-74 (2026-01-23) funded EDA at $466 million ($400 million for assistance programs and $66 million for salaries and expenses) and MBDA at $50 million. CRS reports EDA continues to operate with no closeout begun, its staff fell from a 2023 peak of 324 to 190 in June 2026, and no FY2027 Commerce-Justice-Science appropriation had been enacted as of 2026-08-24.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14238, which directs seven entities including MBDA to eliminate non-statutory functions and reduce statutory functions and staff to the minimum required by law. Published in the Federal Register on 2025-03-20.

In Rhode Island v. Trump (D.R.I.), a preliminary injunction covers MBDA, the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service and the Institute of Museum and Library Services; the First Circuit later declined to stay it pending appeal, according to trade press.

Chief Judge John J. McConnell Jr. grants the plaintiff states summary judgment in Rhode Island v. Trump, vacates the implementation of Executive Order 14238 as to MBDA, IMLS, FMCS and USICH, permanently enjoins further implementation for them, and denies as moot a motion to enforce over MBDA's October 2025 layoff notices, which had been rescinded.
timeline.source: U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island

timeline.event: P.L. 119-74 funds EDA at $466 million ($400 million for economic development assistance programs and $66 million for salaries and expenses) and MBDA at $50 million for FY2026, although the request proposed funding only an orderly shutdown of each ($30 million and $7.3 million, per CRS).

Senate Commerce Committee Democrats ask GAO to expand its MBDA review to possible violations of the court orders. Their release states that funding for at least nine MBDA business centers had been terminated or discontinued by 2025-08-29, that reduction-in-force notices went to the 24 remaining employees on 2025-10-10 and were later rescinded after Congress required it, and that only five of about 40 employees remained after the order took effect (a partisan release; claims are attributed to its authors).
EDA publishes a final rule removing three sections of its general terms and conditions for investment assistance (13 CFR part 302), describing it as a deregulatory action under Executive Order 14192.
CRS reports the FY2027 request again proposes closing EDA ($20 million) and MBDA ($3.5 million) through orderly shutdown funding, against FY2026 enacted levels of $466 million and $50 million.

CRS reports the House committee FY2027 bill would provide $323 million for EDA, the House (July) and Senate (August) passed differing continuing resolutions running to 2026-12-04 and 2026-12-11, EDA has not begun a closeout (EDA estimated seven years to close about 2,300 open grants), and EDA staff stood at 190 in June 2026 versus a 2023 peak of 324.

title: Abolish or consolidate the Economic Development Administration and refocus MBDA
uncertainties: The 2025-11-21 memorandum and order (ECF 99) was read on CourtListener for its holding and relief; whether the government appealed it and with what result was not confirmed on a First Circuit source (a secondary case tracker describes the appeal as ongoing). Executive Order 14238 and the Division A funding lines of P.L. 119-74 were read on primary hosts; the last part of the public law text was not read. The Senate Commerce Committee minority release is a partisan source; its staffing, grant and reduction-in-force details were not independently confirmed. Current MBDA staffing, grants and MBDA FY2027 appropriations action were not verified. EDA staffing figures come from CRS and do not state the cause of the decline. EDA's internal consolidation of decisions and use of direct-hire authority were not verified. An earlier version of the record described three EDA rules covering investment-assistance, public works and planning regulations; the Federal Register page opened on 2026-10-23 shows one rule amending part 302, so the public works and planning rules are an unverified lead.
